creator: Christos Chatzichristos, Dimitris Katsimpokis, Congting Lai, Lore Van Santvliet, Flavio Camarrone, Daan Knoors, Gijs Geleijnse, Michel Van Speybroek, Martine Lewi, Bart Vannieuwenhuyse, Maarten De Vos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe creation of synthetic data in healthcare research has emerged as a compelling solution to address challenges related to data privacy, in case of data-sharing and data scarceness for training machine learning models.ObjectiveThe current paper aims to provide a critical landscape analysis of synthetic data quality metrics used in healthcare, mapping the state of the field, examining how current fidelity and utility scores often fail to capture weaknesses that appear in specific patient subgroups, and illustrating these blind spots with a lung-cancer

title: The Wnt signaling networks in higher-grade meningiomas: from molecular pathogenesis to therapeutic innovation
creator: Arathy S Kumar, Olli Tynninen, Miikka Korja
description: Meningiomas are the most frequently reported primary brain and other central nervous system tumors and account for more than one-third of all primary CNS tumors. High-grade meningiomas (WHO grades 2 and 3) are associated with significantly poorer prognosis and a higher risk of recurrence than grade 1 tumors, despite surgery and radiotherapy.

title: Rituximab and corticosteroids for M-protein-negative PGNMID: case report
creator: Zhuolin Huang, Shuopeng Yang, Jun Cai, Fengying Tang
description: BackgroundWe report a case of a 69-year-old patient negative for serum M-protein who was diagnosed with proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) via renal biopsy.Case presentationA 69-year-old male presented with hematuria, edema, and rapidly progressive renal failure. Serum M-protein was negative, but renal biopsy confirmed IgG3-κ PGNMID with intense C3 deposition and an MPGN-like pattern.

title: Investigating long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) HOTAIR expression changes in ischemic stroke patients
creator: Alia Saberi, Niloufar Nabavi, Amirreza Ghayeghran, Zivar Salehi, Yaser Moaddabi, Mohammad Ebrahim Ghaffari, Haniyeh Haghanipor, Sara Khoshdooz, Ali Bonyad
description: BackgroundIschemic stroke (IS), a leading global health problem, is caused by interrupted blood flow in the brain, often due to clotting or artery constriction. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), particularly HOX transcript antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR), are pivotal in stroke pathophysiology.AimThis study focused on the expression levels of HOTAIR lncRNA in ischemic stroke patients.

title: Aerobic exercise modulates macrophage polarization and promotes cardiac recovery after myocardial infarction in rats
creator: Mingyan Zhu, Bing Zhou, Jianye Peng, Kong Chen, Yu Wang, Hao Zeng, Xia Zhang
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the protective effects of aerobic exercise (AE) on cardiac function and myocardial injury in rats with myocardial infarction (MI), as well as its impact on macrophage polarization.MethodsA rat model of chronic post-infarction remodeling was established by ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery, while the Sham group underwent threading without ligation.

title: StitchR-based dual-AAV delivery strategies enable efficient transduction of defined neural cell populations
creator: Nengsong Luo, Yunling Gao, Zengpeng Han, Peng Su, Fuqiang Xu, Kunzhang Lin
description: Dual adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector reconstitution has become an indispensable technique for delivering large genes in neuroscience and gene therapy. A novel technology termed StitchR addresses the challenge of low efficiency in dual-AAV reconstruction, yet related tools enabling targeted gene delivery to specific neural cell populations remain insufficiently developed.

title: Interpretable machine learning model for brain metastasis in breast cancer: a large-scale, multi-center study
creator: Quan Yuan, Yupeng Sha, Rui Yu, Hao Yu, Rongjie Ye, Yi Du, Hanqing Deng, Liqun Wang, Zhihao Lei, Kaizhou Chen, Jian Cai, Xiaoming Li, Yixin Liu, Yige Lu, Hui Pang, Shuiliang Wang, Taozhu Ye, Youzhuang Wu, Xiaofeng Li, Zhengda Chen, Junjing Li, Shuqi Yang, Kangni Chen, Qinpei Ke, Yongxuan Yuan, Lierui
description: BackgroundBrain metastasis (BM) is a devastating complication of breast cancer (BC) with a poor prognosis. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential but currently lacks accurate predictive tools. This study aimed to develop a stable machine learning model for predicting BM in a large, diverse patient population.

title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal that THBS1 induces radiation resistance in TNBC through the interaction between myCAF and TOPBP1⁺ tumor cells
creator: Fuzhong Liu, Xing Xu, Wenhao Tong, Yang Xie, Yecheng Ma, Lingling Yang, Xun Jin
description: BackgroundRadiation resistance remains a clinical challenge in the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and its mechanisms are not yet fully understood.MethodsWe integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and prognostic data to perform analyses such as intercellular communication, pseudo-temporal trajectories, and GSEA and validated the results using experiments including qPCR, single-cell sequencing and flow cytometry.

title: Non-suicidal self-injury and digital ostracism: a novel smartphone-based paradigm capturing real-time responses to social media exclusion
creator: Carlos Schmidt, Stella Nicolaou, Daniela Otero, Josep Marco-Pallarés, Diana Castilla, Irene Zaragoza, Joaquim Soler, Juan Carlos Pascual, Daniel Vega
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundOstracism on social media is a common and emotionally salient stressor. However, its moment-to-moment psychological and behavioral consequences, remain poorly understood in individuals with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury (NSSI) and Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD).MethodsUsing an Instagram-mimicking smartphone platform (Socializapp) coupled with Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), we examined responses to experimentally manipulated peer feedback across 7 days in three groups: healthy Controls (HC; n = 20), NSSI without BPD (NSSI; n = 18), and comorbid BPD+NSSI (n = 17).

title: The clinical significance of the modified Naples prognostic score for prostate cancer: a population-based study
creator: Hong Zeng, Fan Yang, Qian Wang, Tianyi Zhang, Junhao Chen, Shijie Jin, Tianrui Feng, Zhen Liang, Yuliang Chen, Zhiwei Xie, Chenhui Tang, Zhien Zhou, Yi Zhou, Weigang Yan
description: PurposeThe Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) is a widely recognized scoring system used to assess inflammation and nutrition status, yet its role in prostate cancer (PCa) remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the association between the modified NPS (MNPS) and PCa prevalence and mortality outcomes among participants with self-reported PCa.

title: Iron homeostasis landscape informs patient survival and neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in cancer
creator: Xiaoqing Fan, Kangna Cao, Xu Steven Xu, Xiaoyu Yan
description: BackgroundCancer cells frequently alter iron metabolism by increasing uptake or decreasing export, promoting oncogenesis and proliferation. However, the quantitative relationship between iron homeostasis and cancer remains underexplored.Methods and resultsWe simplified these alterations into measurable changes in the expression levels of iron transport-related genes.

title: Single cell RNA sequencing and emerging transcriptomic technologies in Alzheimer’s disease cerebral organoids: a mini review
creator: Maizatul Fazilah Abdul Razak, Francis Yew Fu Tieng
description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the most common cause of dementia worldwide, presents a formidable challenge due to its complex, multifactorial etiology, and limited translational success of existing models. Recent advances in stem cell biology have enabled the generation of three-dimensional human cerebral organoids which exhibit multicellular complexity and self-organisation, recapitulating key aspects of fetal brain development in vitro.

title: Sensory impairment, loneliness, and the emergence of physical–psychological–cognitive multimorbidity: a cross-national cohort study in China, the United States, and England
creator: Yilin Pan, Jingru Bi, Lili Sun, Long Feng, Rui Wang, Junru Qu, Beibei Du
description: BackgroundThe co-occurrence of physical diseases, psychological disorders, and cognitive impairment—here termed physical–psychological–cognitive multimorbidity (PPC-M)—poses growing challenges to healthy aging but its upstream, modifiable determinants remain underexplored. Sensory impairments are common in later life and may be associated with the emergence of PPC-M, partly through psychosocial factors such as loneliness.

title: Palliative Care education in undergraduate pharmacy curricula in Brazil: a descriptive cross-sectional study
creator: Ricardo Augusto dos Santos Silva, Maria Clara Pedrosa Ferreira, Giovana Flora Martine Teixeira, João Pedro Vasconcelos Paolinelli, Alexandre Ernesto Silva, Mariana Linhares Pereira
description: BackgroundPalliative Care is essential for improving the quality of life of individuals with life-threatening conditions. Despite its growing relevance, the education of health professionals in this field remains insufficient. In Brazil, the implementation of the National Policy for Palliative Care reinforces the need to qualify the health workforce.

title: Knowledge and attitudes toward epilepsy among medical students and internship doctors: a multinational cross-sectional study in Syria, Jordan, Palestine, and Libya
creator: Hamdah Hanifa, Amar Haj Hussin Shehadah, Feras Hamesh, Lujain Alzoubi, Carolin Maksoud, Leen Alfrra, Maya Alzoubi, Fadiah Albaroudi, Batoul Aladib, Nirmin Bachlah, Marwa Hujk, Jamal Alkhatib, Maen Alshak, Yihea Mohammad Al-Mashaqbah, Merei Assad, Tarek Farem, Ekram Hassan Hasanin, Raghad Gharaibeh,
description: BackgroundEpilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by sudden abnormal electrical discharges in the brain. More than three-quarters of people with epilepsy live in developing countries, where the disorder continues to pose a major public health challenge. There are also various causes of this disease, which may include tumors, infections, genetic factors, or traumas.

title: Correlation of whole-body fat content and its distribution with lumbar fat content under different age, gender and BMI conditions: quantitative analysis of MRI based on deep learning
creator: Junjie Fang, Jiazhen Zhu, Aie Liu, Chuanli Cheng, Chao Zou, Aizhu Sheng, Fang Gan, Bin Chen, Guangyu Tang
description: BackgroundThe correlation between abnormal distribution of systemic fat deposition and fat content in the vertebral body remains unclear, and AI segmentation offers novel approach for large-scale quantitative analysis.ObjectiveTo explore the effects of gender, age, and body mass index on the correlation between whole-body fat content/distribution and lumbar spine fat content using deep learning based MRI quantification technology.

title: Association of adverse childhood experiences patterns with successful aging trajectories: a prospective cohort study
creator: Kunhao Yang, Xin Yang, Hui Fan, Lidan Zheng, Xiangli Zeng
description: BackgroundThe long-term influence of distinct adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) patterns on heterogeneous trajectories of successful aging (SA) remains unclear.MethodsUsing 2011–2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study data from 3,092 community-dwelling older adults (aged ≥ 60), latent class analysis identified four distinct ACE patterns from 13 binary indicators based on exposure probabilities, clinical significance, and prior literature.

title: Refractory rapidly progressive diffuse in-stent restenosis with left main involvement: a case report
creator: Xiaoyan Wang, Haichao Yang, Liqiang Qin, Wei Lu, Lijun Wang, Jianjun Wang, Juan Li, Kaibin Deng, Chenguang Gao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDrug-eluting stents (DES) have significantly reduced the incidence of in-stent restenosis (ISR). However, a subset of patients still develop refractory, rapidly progressive, and diffuse ISR, which poses substantial therapeutic challenges and reflects its complex underlying mechanisms.Case presentationWe report a 46-year-old male who underwent five percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) over five years, with repeated diffuse ISR in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Initial PCI was followed by DCB therapy after first ISR, achieving temporary symptom relief.

title: Association between normal-weight central obesity and cardiometabolic disorders: a longitudinal analysis from health check-up data
creator: Yang Cheng, Hui Zheng, Hongli Yin, Donghua Yin, Hui Wang, Ying Wang
description: BackgroundAlthough several cross-sectional studies have examined the relationship between normal-weight central obesity (NWCO) and the risk of cardiometabolic disorders (CMD), longitudinal evidence from cohort studies is still limited, especially regarding diverse CMD outcomes in Chinese populations.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study by using health examination records from Jiangsu Province Geriatric Hospital.

title: Stella safeguards proteostasis via regulating UBE2D3 translation in the maternal-to-zygotic transition
creator: Guorui Zhang, Minjie Ren, Guangyi Sun, Yilong Zhao, Na Zhang, Qiang Wang, Longsen Han
description: Ubiquitin–proteasome-mediated protein degradation is essential for maternal-to-zygotic transition, yet the maternal factors that safeguard ubiquitin–proteasome function remain unclear. Here, using a Stella-mutant mouse model, we demonstrate that Stella is required for global protein ubiquitination during early embryogenesis. Stella deficiency in oocytes leads to reduced ubiquitinated protein levels, impaired zygotic genome activation, and early developmental arrest.

title: A multicentre phase III clinical trial of dual-epigenetic therapy plus CHOP compared with CHOP in previously untreated patients with peripheral T-cell lymphoma
creator: Chong Wei, Liping Su, Xiaobo Wang, Yang Song, Ningbin Chen, Yuanyan Tang, Aijun Liao, Wei Yang, Zhiming Li, Jing Shen, Daobin Zhou, Wei Zhang
description: This phase 3 multicenter trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding dual epigenetic agents azacitidine and chidamide to CHOP (AC-CHOP) versus CHOP alone in previously untreated peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). A total of 128 patients were enrolled from 9 centers in China and assigned according to participating centers (AC-CHOP, N = 84; CHOP, N = 44).

title: Exome-wide association study reveals common and rare coding variants shaping chronic pain in 327,642 UK biobank participants
creator: Xiang Ao, Goodarz Kolifarhood, Marc Parisien, Andrey Bortsov, Audrey V Grant, Luda Diatchenko
description: BackgroundChronic pain is a major global health burden with a substantial but incompletely understood genetic basis. Although genome-wide association studies have identified multiple common-variant loci for pain-related traits, the contribution of rare coding variants to chronic pain susceptibility, biological mechanisms, and shared architecture across pain phenotypes remains unclear.

title: Self-cascade oxygen-generating hydrogel/nanofibrous membrane composites restore periodontal microenvironment homeostasis
creator: Ye Liang, Fan Yang, Jun Kang, Zijun Chen, Ting Zou, Shaohua Ge, Chengfei Zhang
description: The hypoxic environment of deep periodontal pockets favors the thriving of anaerobic microbes, leading to dysbiosis, tissue destruction, and treatment resistance. Elevating intra-pocket oxygen tension is a fundamental yet unmet need for controlling anaerobic pathogens in deep periodontal pockets. Our previous study demonstrated the therapeutic efficacy of oxygen-releasing hydrogel based on calcium peroxide (CPO) in reducing anaerobic pathogens in vitro.

title: The lived experiences of reproductive-aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a qualitative study
creator: Kaitlyn J Ward, A K Benzley, K L King Stone, E S Wardell, J A Hughes, B M Magnusson
description: BackgroundPCOS is a complex health condition that affects up to 20% females of reproductive age worldwide, and approximately 5 million U.S. females of reproductive aged females. Despite the prevalence of the condition, research on the lived experiences of women with PCOS is limited, particularly in the United States.

title: AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality in rural settings: a systematic review
creator: Joy Aifuobhokhan, Ayodeji Ogunjinmi, Chukwuemeka Abraham Agbarakwe, Deborah Oladunmolu Oduguwa, Annie Peter Essiet, Temitayo Osunkiyesi, Akinbogun Modesire
description: BackgroundMaternal mortality remains disproportionately high in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural settings with limited access to skilled obstetric care. Artificial intelligence and machine learning models offer promise for early risk prediction, yet their methodological rigour, applicability, and deployment feasibility in resource-constrained rural contexts remain inadequately synthesised.

title: Three-dimensional subtalar joint space mapping identifies sinus tarsi–predominant structural compromise in early- versus end-stage varus ankle osteoarthritis
creator: Nan Mei, Hiroaki Kurokawa, Takuma Miyamoto, Norihiro Tsujimoto, Yinghao Li, Yaokuan Ruan, Fei Chang, Akira Taniguchi, Yasuhito Tanaka, Kawamura Kenji
description: ObjectiveSubtalar compensation is increasingly recognized in varus ankle osteoarthritis (OA), yet the breakdown of this compensatory mechanism in advanced disease and the regional degenerative signature within the subtalar joint remain poorly characterized. We applied simulated weight-bearing computed tomography (sWBCT)–based three-dimensional (3D) subtalar joint space width (JSW) mapping to quantify regional structural differences between early- and end-stage disease.

title: Musculoskeletal symptoms and pain-response behaviors among university students in Palestine: a cross-sectional study
creator: Ahmed A Badawi, Obada R Al-Mashad, Mohammad Bdair, Mohammad A Badawi, Lana Malhis, Jana M Daraghmeh
description: BackgroundMusculoskeletal (MSK) symptoms are a major contributor to disability worldwide, and university students may be increasingly affected because of prolonged sedentary behavior, intensive digital-device use, and sustained academic workloads. In Palestine, these risks may be compounded by psychosocial stressors and constrained healthcare access.

title: Current status of anti-obesity medications and performance, an EHR based survey
creator: Xiaoyang Ruan, Rui Li, Liwei Wang, Shuyu Lu, Andrew Wen, Murali Sameer, Hongfang Liu
description: BackgroundWhile randomized clinical trials (RCTs) establish the efficacy of anti-obesity medications (AOMs), their real-world effectiveness, inter-individual variability, and weight regain post discontinuation remain poorly characterized across diverse, large scale populations.MethodsElectronic health records with pharmacy dispensation of obesity or overweight individuals were retrieved from local UT-Physician and nationwide EPIC COSMOS databases.

title: Associations between gastrointestinal symptoms and coexisting symptoms amongst patients in a palliative care unit: a PCOC-based longitudinal study
creator: Ching-Ju Lin, Cheng-Fu Lin, Chun-Li Wang, Ju-En Tsai, Lung-Chun Lee, Pi-Shan Hsu, Wei-Min Chu
description: BackgroundGastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are both common and distressing in patients receiving palliative care, however their relationships with coexisting symptoms and clinical factors, including functional status, clinician-rated problem severity, and palliative care phase, remain unclear in hospice ward settings. The Palliative Care Outcomes Collaboration (PCOC) framework enables for standardized daily symptom assessment and longitudinal evaluation.

title: Efgartigimod-responsive autoimmune peripheral neuropathy with concurrent anti-GM2 IgG and anti-contactin-1 IgG antibodies: a rare case report
creator: Ju Huang, Dan Li, Ruyang He, Jun Wei
description: BackgroundImmune-mediated peripheral neuropathies arise from dysregulated immune responses targeting peripheral nerves. Contactin-1 (CNTN1) antibodies, typically of the IgG4 subclass, are associated with autoimmune nodo/paranodopathies and often respond poorly to intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Anti-GM2 IgG antibodies are rare and are usually linked to complement-mediated axonal injury. The coexistence of these antibodies has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported.

title: The clinical and psychosocial consequences of genomic Multi-Cancer Detection (MCD) tests in underserved populations: a scoping review
creator: Esther Low, Shritha Gayathri, Alexandra Wicker, Amanda Courtright-Lim, Jessica Austin, Jewel Samadder, Steven Ressler, Jon Tilburt
description: IntroductionMulti-cancer detection (MCD) tests currently being tested in clinical trials may be a scalable, convenient means to improve cancer screening, yet little is known about the potential clinical and psychosocial consequences of doing so in underserved communities.ObjectiveTo summarize the current literature examining potential clinical and psychosocial outcomes and consequences for MCD testing in underserved populations.

title: MFCAMNet: predicting miRNA-disease associations by multi-feature cascade attention mechanism network
creator: Yuanxing Wang, Chen Yang, Yucheng Zhang
description: Drive by the rapid envolution of deep-learning techniques, a large body of biological experiments bas has uncovered extensive associations between microRNAs (miRNAs) and complex human diseases, hig- hlighting the pivotal roles of miRNAs in pathogenesis. Elucidating these associations is essential for understanding disease mechanisms and developing preventive strategies.

title: Polygenic risk score assessment of LDL-Cholesterol levels and progression to severe hypercholesterolemia and statin treatment; a longitudinal study from a large middle eastern biobank
creator: Umm-Kulthum Ismail Umlai, Salman M Toor, Usama Aliyu, Shaban Mohammed, Nadeem Qureshi, Moza S.H. Al Hail, Mohammed Gomaa, Amin Jayyousi, Jassim M. Al Suwaidi, Omar M.E. Albagha
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2027). major modifiable risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and affects approximately 20% of the global population [1]. LDL-C is influenced by monogenic, polygenic, lifestyle and environmental factors. Over 120 LDL-C polygenic scores (PGS) are listed in the PGS Catalog [2], but most were developed in European or predominantly European datasets, and their performance can be reduced in other ancestries because of differences in linkage disequilibrium, allele frequencies and effect sizes [3].

title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor as a molecular mediator in the induction of human aldehyde oxidase gene expression
creator: Szu Ling Yeap, Cassandra Ching Lin Yap, Shi Han Tay, Linghua Harris Zhang, Aik Jiang Lau
description: Relatively little is known about receptor-mediated regulation of aldehyde oxidase (AOX). 2,3,7,8-Tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin, an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) agonist, increases mouse Aox expression. However, given the species differences in ligand-dependent AHR activation and AOX regulation, it remains to be investigated whether human AHR regulates the expression of AOX1 (the human AOX isoform).
